CITI honoured sustainability leaders at the CITI Textile Sustainability Awards 2026 during Bharat Tex in New Delhi, with Union Minister Pabitra Margherita presenting the awards. 
CITI also partnered with SLCP to help MSMEs meet ESG requirements. 
Awards recognised excellence in sustainable manufacturing, energy efficiency, cotton, HR, innovation and academic contributions.

title: EU, India advance cooperation on trade & clean technologies
summary:
EU and India used their third Trade and Technology Council meeting in Brussels to prioritise resilient value chains, market access and business engagement.
Exporters, importers and sourcing teams may see follow-up on technical regulations, digital trust services and standards.
Working groups will report regularly as both sides prepare the next ministerial meeting.

title: ICE cotton gains after two-day decline amid weaker US dollar
summary:
ICE cotton futures rebounded after a two-day decline, with the December 2026 contract settling 0.68 cent higher at 81.55 cents per pound, supported by a weaker US dollar, stronger crude oil prices, and commodity markets.
Traders remained focused on West Texas weather, China's reserve auction, and US export demand, while ICE-certified cotton stocks declined, indicating tighter deliverable supplies.

title: India's carbon market hands textile exporters a future CBAM edge
summary:
India has placed 173 large textile units under the Indian Carbon Market, with verified Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions due by July 31, 2026.
For exporters, one verified dataset can support domestic compliance, future CBAM claims and European Union Digital Product Passport reporting.
Non-compliance can attract compensation of twice the carbon-credit price, adding working-capital pressure for mills.

title: Vietnam experts back faster policy rollout for growth stability
summary:
To tackle global uncertainties, Vietnam should improve the quality of growth, boost economic resilience and speed up implementation of existing policies, economic experts suggest. 
While growth figures reflect positive short-term results, long-term success would depend not only on the pace of growth, but also on the quality and resilience of the economy and the sustainability of growth engines, they feel.

title: Bharat Tex 2026 Day 2 drives focus on state-led growth & global trade
summary:
Bharat Tex 2026 Day 2 highlighted the role of state governments, FTAs and global partnerships in strengthening India's textile industry. 
Sessions by Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra showcased investment opportunities, while discussions on India-UK CETA, global value chains, retail expansion and resilient supply chains focused on boosting exports, manufacturing and global competitiveness.

title: Texworld NYC marks 20 years with expanded Summer 2026 sourcing event
summary:
Texworld NYC's 20th anniversary edition will bring together Texworld, Apparel Sourcing, Home Textiles Sourcing and Printsource under one roof from July 29-31.
Featuring 425+ exhibitors, the event combines global sourcing, trend forecasting, sustainability, AI-focused discussions and technical workshops, strengthening its role as a leading North American textile sourcing platform.

title: India’s LMW receives strong response at Bharat Tex 2026
summary:
LMW Limited drew strong visitor interest on Day 2 of Bharat Tex 2026, reflecting robust demand for its textile machinery solutions.
President – Operations S. Rajasekaran highlighted the importance of ecosystem-driven manufacturing during an India ITME Society panel on textile machinery.
The company continues to reinforce its leadership through innovation, industry engagement and customer-focused solutions.

title: WILEYTEX launches salt-free cotton dyeing with 90% water savings
summary:
Taiwan's WILEYTEX Technology has launched ecoloration, a proprietary cotton dyeing technology that reduces water consumption by up to 90 per cent, energy use and carbon emissions by 80 per cent.
Commercially validated in Eswatini, the technology delivers up to eight times higher throughput than conventional dyeing and targets brands and manufacturers seeking lower-impact, compliant cotton supply chains.

title: DGFT unveils Brand India initiative, T&A among priority sectors
summary:
India's DGFT has launched 'Niryat Disha' under the Export Promotion Mission to strengthen global branding, packaging, and labelling of Indian exports, with textiles and apparel among the priority sectors.
The initiative proposes a Unified Brand India framework, a voluntary Trust Mark, branding support, and funding of up to ₹10 crore per project, with stakeholder consultations open for 30 days.

title: Cambodia's H1 2026 apparel exports up 5.7%; cotton imports surge
summary:
Cambodia's apparel exports rose 5.7 per cent year on year to $5.55 billion in the first half of 2026, accounting for 32.5 per cent of the country's total merchandise exports.
Growth was led by non-knitted apparel, while imports of cotton and cotton yarn surged 34.8 per cent, signalling stronger demand for cotton-based garment production.

title: Bangladesh’s EU export decline points to a shift in apparel sourcing
summary:
BKMEA says H&M’s Bangladesh orders are ~40 per cent lower YoY, while FY26 apparel exports fell 1.64 per cent, led by a 3.31 per cent drop in EU shipments. 
Germany’s imports from Bangladesh fell 11.5 per cent ($570 million), driving most of the country’s $645 million export decline. 
India gains with UK tariff-free access, a pending EU FTA, and ₹95,000 crore in planned textile investments.

title: Africa’s apparel exporters have less than six months of certainty
summary:
Africa’s apparel exports reached $8.62 billion in 2025, but AGOA’s expiry in 170 days is limiting long-term investment despite supporting current orders.
While short-term renewals preserve production, uncertainty is delaying textile value-chain expansion, leaving key exporting hubs such as Lesotho vulnerable and slowing deeper industrial development.

title: US tariffs favour cotton, yet it loses in 6 of 8 categories
summary:
TexPro’s $9.97-billion analysis shows cotton lost value share in six of eight matched apparel categories in Q1 2026, despite its tariff advantage over man-made fibres.
Performance requirements, cost competitiveness and preferential trade agreements continue to sustain synthetic apparel demand, suggesting sourcing is shifting by geography rather than through broad fibre substitution.

title: PDS, Busana Apparel to build next gen of global apparel manufacturing
summary:
PDS Limited has partnered with Indonesia's Busana Apparel Group to strengthen its global manufacturing ecosystem.
The alliance expands their combined manufacturing footprint across Asia, Central America and Europe, enabling greater production scale, supply chain resilience, faster speed-to-market and enhanced support for global fashion brands seeking diversified sourcing.

title: India's textile exports rise, apparel exports decline in June 2026
summary:
India's textile and apparel exports rose a marginal 0.21 per cent YoY to $2.91 billion in June 2026 as higher textile shipments offset weaker apparel exports.
However, exports fell 2.95 per cent during April–June and 2.21 per cent in FY26, while raw cotton imports surged amid continued pressure from weak global demand and higher costs.

title: Indonesia & Cambodia lead the shift in US apparel sourcing
summary:
US apparel imports fell 9.3 per cent in January–May 2026, but Cambodia (+15% value, +18% volume) and Indonesia (+5.5%, +13%) expanded market share. 
Bangladesh remained the No. 2 supplier, yet exports fell 8.1 per cent by value and 6.2 per cent by volume. 
China’s exports plunged 42.8 per cent, with sourcing shifting mainly to Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam.

title: China’s apparel got cheaper but US imports still fell 42.8%
summary:
US apparel imports from China fell 42.8 per cent in January–May 2026 despite China offering the lowest average import value at $1.43 per SME.
Buyers increasingly prioritised tariff certainty, compliance and supply-chain resilience over cost, shifting orders to higher-priced sourcing markets while using China’s low benchmark to negotiate elsewhere.

title: Cambodia, ILO review draft workplace safety law
summary:
Cambodia has advanced its first comprehensive occupational safety and health law after a tripartite consultation in Phnom Penh.
The draft consolidates more than 20 existing legal instruments, signalling a potential compliance shift for employers and sourcing teams.
The ILO-backed process seeks alignment with international labour standards and stronger workplace safety systems.
